short_title: Laken Riley Act

parts.description: Noncitizens who are inadmissible and are charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admit to theft, burglary, larceny, shoplifting, assault of a police officer, or a crime causing death or serious injury.
The Homeland Security Secretary must issue a detainer and take the person into custody; detention becomes mandatory rather than discretionary.
Department of Homeland Security (ICE).
A state attorney general may sue the federal government for harm to the state or its residents caused by certain immigration release and parole decisions.
Takes effect on enactment; no phase-in.

daily_life: Changes whether a noncitizen arrested for shoplifting stays in federal custody while the case proceeds.

short_title: Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025

parts.description: Continues federal agency funding for the rest of fiscal year 2025 at roughly prior-year rates, with listed exceptions (anomalies).
Funding runs to the end of the fiscal year.
Replaces a short-term stopgap with a full-year continuing resolution instead of twelve regular appropriations bills.
Extends several expiring programs and authorities (extenders) to a new date.

daily_life: Keeps federal offices, parks and benefit processing open for the rest of the fiscal year.

short_title: Disapproval of IRS digital-asset broker reporting rule

parts.description: Congress disapproves an agency rule under the Congressional Review Act; the rule has no force or effect.
Decentralized finance platforms that would have been treated as brokers required to report gross proceeds of digital-asset sales.
A one-sentence law: it names the rule by its Federal Register citation and voids it.

daily_life: Crypto users on decentralized platforms do not get new IRS forms from those platforms.
notes: Congressional Review Act resolutions are a distinct federal instrument: a repeal of a regulation, not a statute.

short_title: Disapproval of CFPB overdraft lending rule

parts.description: Voids the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule on overdraft lending by very large financial institutions.
Banks and credit unions with more than $10 billion in assets (the rule's scope).
The voided rule would have capped overdraft fees (for example at $5 or at cost); that cap never takes effect.

daily_life: Large banks may keep charging their existing overdraft fees.

short_title: TAKE IT DOWN Act (Tools to Address Known Exploitation by Immobilizing Technological Deepfakes on Websites and Networks Act)
effective_dates: platform notice-and-removal process due 1 year after enactment

parts.description: Knowingly publishing nonconsensual intimate images, including computer-generated 'digital forgeries', is a federal crime.
Prison terms up to about 2 years when the victim is an adult and about 3 years when a minor.
Covered online platforms must set up a process to receive removal requests and remove the image within 48 hours of a valid request.
Platforms get one year to build the removal process.
Failure to comply with removal duties is treated as an unfair or deceptive practice enforced by the Federal Trade Commission.

daily_life: A person can make a platform take down a fake explicit image of them within two days.

short_title: Disapproval of EPA waiver for California Advanced Clean Trucks

parts.description: Voids the EPA decision that had waived federal preemption for California's heavy-truck emission standards.
With the waiver gone, federal preemption of state vehicle emission standards applies again to these California rules.
Heavy-duty truck makers selling in California and states that adopted California's standards.

daily_life: Truck buyers in California and follower states are not required to see a rising share of zero-emission trucks.

short_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act - no tax on tips and overtime deductions

parts.description: New deduction for qualified tips received in tipped occupations.
New deduction for the premium part of required overtime pay.
Deductions phase down for higher earners.
Both deductions are temporary.
Employers must report tips and overtime separately on wage statements.

daily_life: A server who earns $15,000 in tips can deduct it from federal taxable income through 2028.

short_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act - Medicaid community engagement requirement
effective_dates: states must start by the first quarter beginning after 2026-12-31; waivers can delay

parts.description: Adults in the Medicaid expansion group, roughly ages 19 to 64, with exemptions.
Must show at least 80 hours a month of work, community service, a work program, or school (or income equal to that).
Exempts groups such as parents of young children, medically frail people, and some others.
States start no later than the first quarter after December 31, 2026, with a limited good-faith delay option.
State Medicaid agencies verify compliance under federal HHS rules.

daily_life: A 40-year-old on expansion Medicaid must document 80 hours of monthly activity or lose coverage.

short_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act - SNAP state cost share by error rate
effective_dates: benefit cost share starts fiscal year 2028 (inferred)

parts.description: States pay part of SNAP benefit costs, set by their payment error rate.
The state share of SNAP administrative costs rises.
Benefit cost share begins a few years after enactment.

daily_life: If a state processes SNAP cases badly, its own budget pays more of every family's food benefit.

short_title: HALT Fentanyl Act (Halt All Lethal Trafficking of Fentanyl Act)

parts.description: Places fentanyl-related substances as a class permanently in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.
Brings these substances under the existing mandatory minimum sentences keyed to drug weight.
Streamlines registration for researchers studying Schedule I substances.
Replaces a temporary class-wide scheduling order with permanent law.

daily_life: Trafficking look-alike fentanyl compounds carries the same mandatory prison terms as fentanyl.

short_title: GENIUS Act (Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act)
effective_dates: earlier of 18 months after enactment or 120 days after final regulations (inferred)

parts.description: Only permitted payment stablecoin issuers may issue payment stablecoins to U.S. persons.
Issuers must hold reserves backing outstanding coins one-to-one in cash, deposits or short Treasuries.
Issuers above a size limit fall under federal supervision; smaller ones may choose a qualifying state regime.
Monthly public reports of reserve composition, examined by an accountant.
Federal banking regulators (OCC, Fed, FDIC) and state regulators.
Delayed start tied to regulations.

daily_life: A dollar stablecoin in a phone wallet must be backed by real dollars or Treasuries held by a licensed issuer.

short_title: Rescissions Act of 2025

parts.description: Cancels previously appropriated, unspent budget authority.
About $9 billion in total, mostly foreign aid accounts plus public broadcasting funds.
Moves under the Impoundment Control Act after a presidential rescission request.

touches: State Department and foreign aid programs
daily_life: Local public radio stations lose federal grant money they expected.

short_title: Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026

parts.description: Three full-year appropriations bills (Agriculture-FDA, Legislative Branch, Military Construction-VA) plus a stopgap for everything else.
Stopgap funding for other agencies to a date in early 2026.
Ends a lapse in appropriations (government shutdown) and provides back pay for furloughed workers.
Extends expiring programs (extenders).

daily_life: Federal workers go back to work and get back pay; food assistance resumes on schedule.

short_title: Epstein Files Transparency Act

parts.description: The Attorney General must publish, in searchable form, unclassified Justice Department records about a named criminal investigation.
Release within about 30 days of enactment.
Allows withholding of victims' personal information and material that would jeopardize an active investigation.
Report to congressional judiciary committees listing what was withheld and why.

daily_life: The public can read case files that were previously withheld.

short_title: SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act of 2025

parts.description: Reauthorizes opioid prevention, treatment and recovery grant programs with annual funding ceilings.
Program authorizations run through fiscal year 2030.
Grants for prenatal and postnatal care, recovery housing, and first responder training (examples from the table of contents).
HHS and SAMHSA.

daily_life: Keeps federal money flowing to local addiction treatment and recovery programs.

short_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026

parts.description: Authorizes (does not appropriate) defense spending by account in funding tables.

numbers.unit: thousand USD operation and maintenance line total (column reading inferred)
numbers.text: 291544245 thousand USD operation and maintenance line total (column reading inferred)

parts.description: Hundreds of policy provisions on personnel, procurement, bases and reporting.
Many required reports and briefings to the armed services committees.
Most provisions apply for fiscal year 2026.

daily_life: Sets the rules and spending limits the Pentagon operates under for the year.

short_title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025
sub_topic: Food production and safety / school meals

parts.description: Schools in the lunch program must offer a variety of fluid milk and may offer whole, reduced-fat, low-fat and fat-free, flavored or not.
Milk fat is not counted as saturated fat when measuring a meal against the saturated-fat limit.
A parent or guardian (not only a physician) can request a nondairy substitute.
Nondairy beverages must be fortified to cow's-milk levels of calcium, protein, and vitamins A and D.

daily_life: Children can get whole milk with school lunch again.

short_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026

parts.description: Full-year appropriations in divisions: Defense; Labor-HHS-Education; Transportation-HUD; Financial Services; National Security-State.
Most amounts available through September 30, 2026; some multi-year.
Includes community project funding (earmarks) listed in explanatory statements.
Separate divisions extend expiring health programs (health care extenders) and other authorities.

daily_life: Sets this year's funding for schools grants, housing vouchers, highways and the military.

short_title: Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025

parts.description: The FCC must start a rulemaking to create a vetting process for applicants for new high-cost Universal Service Fund broadband awards.
Applicants must show technical, financial and operational capability and a reasonable business plan in the first application.
Technology-neutral evaluation against established standards.

daily_life: Rural areas are less likely to be promised internet by a company that cannot build it.

short_title: Secure America Act (budget reconciliation)

parts.description: Mandatory appropriation to Customs and Border Protection for Border Patrol agents and support staff (non-enforcement functions).
Mandatory appropriation to ICE Homeland Security Investigations, with a set-aside for child-exploitation investigators.
Money stays available for several years.
Money may not be used to hire processing coordinators after a date.
Out of the general Treasury under a budget resolution's reconciliation instructions.

daily_life: Funds more federal agents and investigators without an annual vote.

short_title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
enactment_path: became law without the President's signature

parts.description: Large institutional investors may not buy single-family homes, with listed exceptions.
Build-to-rent, new construction for sale, substantial renovation (at least 15 percent of price), and qualifying rent-to-own programs are excepted.

numbers.unit: percent of purchase price minimum renovation
numbers.text: 15 percent of purchase price minimum renovation

parts.description: No forced sale of homes owned before enactment.
Treasury may write rules but may not change the numeric threshold or definitions.
Homelessness grant recipients may seek waivers of spending caps for fiscal years 2027-2030.
FHA multifamily loan limits indexed to a Census construction price deflator.
New and reauthorized programs, including a HOME program reauthorization and planning grants.
States that no additional funds are authorized by the act.

daily_life: Big investment firms can no longer outbid families for existing starter homes.

short_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027

parts.description: Continues funding at prior-year rates for fiscal year 2027 agencies.
Stopgap runs to a date in December.
Extends expiring authorities to the same date.

daily_life: Avoids a shutdown on October 1.

short_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
sub_topic: Sanctions and export controls / trade and customs

parts.description: Bans on transfers of funds, new investment, sovereign debt purchases, securities listings and energy exports involving Russia.
Duties on all goods imported from Russia raised to up to 500 percent ad valorem, on top of other duties.
Duties up to 100 percent on goods from countries that buy Russian oil or gas or help evade sanctions.
President must act within 30 days of enactment.
Presidential waiver and termination on certification to Congress.
Main division ends five years after enactment.
Division B, unrelated: extends the educator expense deduction to early childhood educators.

daily_life: Some imported goods get sharply more expensive; banks block certain transfers.

short_title: Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023

parts.description: Suspends the statutory debt limit until January 1, 2025.
Statutory discretionary spending caps for fiscal years 2024 and 2025.
Raises the SNAP able-bodied adult time-limit age range in steps, while adding exemptions for veterans, homeless people and former foster youth.
The SNAP changes expire.
Rescinds unobligated COVID-era funds.
Environmental review page and time limits: about 1 year for assessments, 2 years for impact statements.

daily_life: Avoided a federal default; some adults on SNAP face work rules longer into their 50s.

short_title: Security supplemental with Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act

parts.description: Emergency security aid for Ukraine, Israel and the Indo-Pacific.
App stores and hosting services may not distribute a foreign-adversary-controlled app unless it is divested.
Defines a 'foreign adversary controlled application', naming one company by name.

daily_life: Raised the prospect that a popular video app would disappear from phones unless sold.

short_title: FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024

parts.description: Authorizes FAA programs and airport grants for fiscal years 2024-2028.
Air traffic controller hiring targets and safety programs.
Codifies automatic cash refunds to passengers for cancelled or significantly delayed flights.
Airport Improvement Program grants to airports.

daily_life: If a flight is cancelled, the refund arrives without a fight.

short_title: Fire Grants and Safety Act (includes ADVANCE Act of 2024)
sub_topic: Electricity and the grid - nuclear licensing

parts.description: Lowers the hourly fees the Nuclear Regulatory Commission charges advanced-reactor applicants.
Prizes for the first advanced reactor licensed and other firsts.
Reauthorizes firefighter grant programs (AFG, SAFER) and the U.S. Fire Administration.
NRC; FEMA / U.S. Fire Administration.

daily_life: Local fire departments keep competing for federal equipment and staffing grants.

short_title: American Relief Act, 2025

parts.description: Disaster relief appropriations of about $100 billion after hurricanes.
Economic assistance payments to farmers per acre of commodity planted.
Extends the 2018 farm bill programs another year.
Stopgap funding for the government into March.

daily_life: Farmers get a per-acre payment; hurricane-hit towns get rebuilding money.

short_title: Senator Elizabeth Dole 21st Century Veterans Healthcare and Benefits Improvement Act

parts.description: Raises the cap on VA spending for home care from a share of nursing home cost to the full cost.
Expands caregiver, homelessness and survivor benefits across many sections.
Department of Veterans Affairs.

daily_life: An aging veteran can get more hours of care at home instead of moving to a nursing home.

short_title: EXPLORE Act (Expanding Public Lands Outdoor Recreation Experiences Act)

parts.description: Land agencies must improve recreation access, data and permits on federal land.
Moves toward digital recreation passes and simpler outfitter permits.
Visitors to national parks, forests and other federal lands, including people with disabilities.

daily_life: Easier to buy a park pass online and get a guide permit.

short_title: Thomas R. Carper Water Resources Development Act of 2024

parts.description: Authorizes specific Army Corps of Engineers projects with cost ceilings.
Projects require a non-federal cost share from a local sponsor.
Directs feasibility studies before construction.

daily_life: Lets a town's levee or harbor project move into the federal pipeline.

short_title: Social Security Fairness Act of 2023
effective_dates: benefits payable for months after December 2023

parts.description: Repeals the Windfall Elimination Provision and the Government Pension Offset.
Retirees who also receive a pension from work not covered by Social Security, such as some teachers and police.
Retroactive to benefits payable after December 2023.

daily_life: A retired teacher sees a larger Social Security check and a lump-sum back payment.
